I've been farming this land since I was young. Quzhou is flat, good soil, but dry — we depend on the well for water. My family has about 8 mu. My husband helps during the busy season but works construction most of the year, so I manage most of this myself.

The only real choice here is wheat and maize, same rotation as always, same as everyone in the village. I tried vegetables once years ago — too much work, too hard to sell, the price collapsed. Wheat and maize I know, the grain station buys them, I can predict what I'll get.

For wheat I'll buy improved seeds from the township supply cooperative, the kind the extension station recommends — my neighbor used Jimai 22 last year and her yield was decent. I'll apply base fertilizer before planting: diammonium phosphate mixed with urea, top-dress urea again in spring at jointing. Three irrigations: the winter water before the ground freezes, again at jointing in April, once more near heading in May. I'll spray herbicide in autumn and again in spring, and do one fungicide spray for powdery mildew.

For maize I'll use hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 or whatever the seed shop has, everyone uses hybrid now. I plant straight into the wheat stubble — no time for tillage, wheat comes off in June and I need to get maize in the ground fast. Two irrigations if it doesn't rain, herbicide once, and one spray for corn borer in July.

I won't change what works. My back isn't what it was and I can't afford to gamble on something unfamiliar.
